text: Lump in groin that gets bigger when standing/coughing/passing stool and any of: severe pain, vomiting, no stools or flatus/wind for past 24 hours, or lump cannot be reduced: incarcerated/strangulated inguinal hernia likely

detail.problem: Part (d) is encoded as an AND of two 24-hour findings: constipation with onset >= 24 hours ago AND unable to break wind with onset >= 24 hours ago. The page lists 'no stools or flatus/wind for past 24 hours' as one item in an 'any of' list, i.e. either absence qualifies; requiring both is stricter than the page, so a patient with 24 hours of no stools but who can still pass wind (or vice versa) does not reach the probable diagnosis and the Urgent priority. The other parts are correct: (a) Groin mass + Cough impulse of mass present (a reasonable proxy for 'gets bigger when standing/coughing/passing stool'; the standing/straining components are not separately represented but the SNOMED cough-impulse concept is the standard sign for a reducible hernia); (b) Severe pain; (c) Finding of vomiting; (e) Groin mass with Irreducible qualifier; (f) two probable rules, Irreducible inguinal hernia and Strangulated inguinal hernia, with identical evidence, which matches the page's 'incarcerated/strangulated' wording. The 'past 24 hours' is approximated with Constipation onset >= 24 hours ago; the language cannot say 'no stool passed', so this is the closest available.
